question: Should fs-safe 0.5 permanently replace the operational Python-helper path with optional native packages plus guarded JavaScript fallbacks, and adopt the accompanying nine-package publishing model?
rationale: This is a public release-contract choice: it intentionally changes required-helper behavior, adds several public APIs and package artifacts, and cannot be resolved by a mechanical code repair.

options.title: Sponsor the 0.5 migration
options.body: Approve the native-only direction and package topology after a final maintainer review of the migration guide, npm trusted-publisher setup, and compatibility promises.

options.title: Preserve a longer compatibility path
options.body: Request a maintained Python compatibility mode or a different deprecation window before accepting the release contract.

options.title: Split the release
options.body: Land only independently approved primitives and defer the native-package migration and release-pipeline changes to a narrower follow-up.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the 0.5 migration
recommendation.body: Approve the native-only direction and package topology after a final maintainer review of the migration guide, npm trusted-publisher setup, and compatibility promises.
